lineas.texto: Part three. It is August, and the whole village is out in the fields.
This is the most important month of the year. If the harvest fails, there is no bread until next summer.
Everyone helps. Men cut the wheat with sickles. Women and children tie it into sheaves.
The lord takes his share. The church takes a tenth, called the tithe.
The poorest families may gather the grain left on the ground. This is called gleaning.
On the days you work the lord's harvest, he must feed you. Bread, cheese, and ale.
And when the work is done, there is music by the fire.
You fall asleep tired, on your bed of straw. Tomorrow, it all starts again.
Could you live one year like this?
